universalIdentityRules: Cosmetic revisions, renamed variables, reordered equivalent expressions, duplicate mathematical tasks and changed option lists share exposure lineage at every difficulty.
A new immutable revision of an existing problem ID retains attempted history, including when the change is substantive; it cannot count as unseen solely because its revision changed.
Cross-topic or cross-level copies share identity/idea aliases where independently reviewed. Reclassification never erases an established alias.
The same reviewed mappings apply to the pinned baseline and candidate. Main evaluation counts deduplicated eligible lineages.
instanceVersusIdea: A parameter change never establishes a new independent idea. A distinct numerical calculation can be a useful elementary fluency instance in the same family and idea group. Record those counts separately.
advancedQualification: For meaningful advanced planning and headroom, independently review normalized tasks and collapse pure scale, affine-coordinate, or finite-prefix copies that add no advanced decision. Keep the reason and exact finite mapping. Useful variants should change hypotheses, geometry, boundaries, cases, or substantive computations.
lowerFluencyScope: Lower-level parameter-specific tasks may retain distinct exposure identities when each asks a distinct numerical calculation and is reviewed as useful practice. They do not increase independent-idea counts, cannot bypass the real family cap, and still need the actual repeated-session and option-quality gates. This is not blanket approval for arbitrary coefficient generation.
notAnEquivalenceProof: A shared broad method alone does not make two numerical items identical. Conversely, a different ID or answer alone does not prove meaningful novelty. The review records the concrete correspondence and distinguishes identity, construction, related idea, structure and primary method.
coverageStatus: Final per-item aliases, qualified group totals, and cap-effective capacities remain pending independent content review. No complete-horizon result is claimed by this policy.
